April 1, 1926
REPORT ON Return of Kubiak and Lepse
Made by P. O. O. Kedrolivansky Forwarded by H. Smeeton B. D. S.
Sir,
Further to my report dated March 22, 1926,
V. S. Kubiak and I. I. Lepse came here from Canton by the
s.s. "Pamiat Lenina" on March 31, and are now living in the
Soviet Consulate. Kubiak and Lepse were met on arrival
by Elleder and Kargalsky, members of the staff of the
Soviet Mercantile Fleet, Wilde, Soviet Vice Consul, and Sorokin,
member of the Soviet Trade Mission.
I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
V. Kedrolivansky
P. O. O.
D. C. I.

March 25, 6.

Dear Blackburn,

Further to my letter of March 22,
I forward herewith a photograph of a group of
persons whose names reading from left to right
are:-

Kubiak, member of Head Committee of
Russian Communistic Party and Secretary of its Far
Eastern Committee; also member of Commission which
inspected Soviet Consulate.

Gamaruk, Chief of the Far Eastern
Committee of the Russian Communistic Party.

Gamaruk's wife.

Fedoroff, Secretary of Manchurian
Committee of the Russian Communistic Party and
editor of the Harbin newspaper "Echo".

Vladimiroff, Secretary of Communistic
Committee on Chinese Eastern Railway.

Solovieff, Secretary of Peking Embassy
and Deputy of Karahan: also member of Mission which
inspected Soviet Consulate.

Yours sincerely,

(Sd.) E.I.M. Barrett.

A. D. Blackburn, Esquire,
H. B. M. Consulate-General,
Shanghai.

CENTRAL I. O. Station.

March 22, 1926.

REPORT ON Identity of Members of Mission which
Inspected Soviet Consulate.

Made by P.C.C. Kedrolivansky Forwarded by J.McEwen C.S.D.

Sir,

Further to the report dated March 22, relative
to the Mission which came here to inspect the Soviet
Consulate, I am attaching herewith a photograph of a
group of persons whose names reading from left to
right are:

1/ Mr. Kubiak - Member of Head Committee of Russian
Communistic Party and Secretary of its
Far Eastern Committee. (member of the
above Mission)

2/ Mr. Gamaruk - Chief of the Far Eastern Committee of
the R. C. P.

3/ Wife of above, No. 2.

4/ Mr. Fedoroff - Secretary of Manchurian Committee
of the R. C. P. and Editor of the
Harbin newspaper "Echo".

5/ Vladimiroff - Secretary of Communistic Committee on
Chinese Eastern Railway.

6/ Mr. Solovieff - Secretary of Peking Embassy and
Deputy of Karahan. (member of the
above Mission).

The description given in Mr. Blackburn's letter
of March 11, tallies with that of the 2nd secretary of
the Soviet Consulate, whose name is I.N. Chusoff.
Although Chusoff has the appearance of a Jew he is really
a Rumanian.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant
V. Kedrolivansky
P. C. C.

D. C. I.

March 22, 6.

Dear Blackburn,

With reference to your letter of March 11, enquiries show that five Soviet officials named N. A. Kubiak, Solovieff, Karpenko, Kalakutis and Kazetzky arrived in Shanghai about March 2. They put up at the Soviet Consulate and left for Nanking by train on March 12. While here, they made a complete investigation into the work of the Consulate and are reported to have suggested some changes for the purpose of increasing efficiency. They intend to conduct similar inspections at all Soviet Consulates in Eastern China.

✓ Kubiak, who is the leader of the Mission and who is responsible direct to Moscow, is about 48 years old, of medium height and build, has a fair complexion and sometimes wears pince nez glasses when reading. He is typically Russian and would never be mistaken for a Jew.

✓ Solovieff, who represents the Peking Embassy in the Mission, is about 5 feet 9 inches in height, medium build, blond hair brushed back, blue eyes, wears gold pince nez spectacles and is about 35 years old.

Karpenko, who is a member of the Cheka in Vladivostock, is Kubiak's bodyguard while Kalakutis acts as his secretary. Kazetzky is attached to the Mission as special messenger.

Kubiak is a native of Ukraine, Solovieff is a Russian, Karpenko belongs to the Crimea, Kalakutis is a Latvian and Kazetsky is a Pole but none of them are Jews.

2.

We know of nobody who answers the
description given in your letter. Efforts are now
being made to obtain photographs of Kubiak and
Solovieff.

Yours sincerely,

(Sd.) E.I.M. Barrett.

A. D. Blackburn, Esquire,
H. B. M. Consulate-General,
Shanghai.

No.____________________
Dated, the 11th March, 1926

Dear Capt.Barrett,

With reference to our conversation this morn-
ing, you will remember that in the memo I showed you, a
Russian was mentioned whose name was not known, but
whose description was as follows: "age about 40, clean
shaven, black eyes, Jewish appearance, below medium
height. Wears rimless pince-nez with gold chain and
ear clip." This man stated that he had recently come
from Peking and was about to return there.

It is possible that he is either SOLOVIEFF
or N.A.KUBIAK, both of whom recently arrived from Peking.
The latter, who is stated in the "New Shanghai Life" of
March 3rd to be a member of the "Dalrevkom" or Far East-
ern Revolutionary Committee, is the most likely. I wonder
if any of your people know what Solovieff and Kubiak look
like and can say whether either of them tallies with the
above description.

Yours sincerely,
A.D.Hackham

Capt.E.I.M.Barrett, C.I.E.,
Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai.
